In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rice grain yields are higher in rotations that include wheat and/or soybean and are lower with continuous rice production.
rice grain yield is improved by using soybean, wheat and corn in a rotation with rice.
the rice corn (soybean) rotation was the best rotation for the 2002 growing season and the conventional till treatment was the best tillage system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rice corn rotation was better than continuous rice, but not as good as the rice corn soybean rotation.
the rice corn rotation with soybeans and wheat as the second phase crops was best.
there were significant increases in rice yields with the addition of wheat in the rice rotation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rice yield can be increased by 20 bu/acre by using a rotation that includes wheat, soybean, corn, or a combination of these crops.
the 3 phase rotation using soybean and wheat as the other two crops in the rotation will provide the best yields.
rice yield can be increased by using wheat as a cover crop in a 3 phase rotation with rice.
